metadata.title: SPARC Azure Application Gateway Component Definition

components.title: Azure Application Gateway v2
components.description: Application Gateway Standard_v2 with TLS termination on port 443, HTTP-to-HTTPS 301 redirect, backend pool targeting the VM private IP, health probe on the application port, and optional SSL certificate. Deployed via Terraform (Azure/VM/modules/app_gateway/). <!-- UPDATE: Insert Application Gateway resource ID, public IP, backend pool details, and SSL certificate name for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for Azure Application Gateway

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity: The Application Gateway terminates TLS on port 443 using an uploaded SSL certificate (dynamic ssl_certificate block). An HTTPS listener accepts encrypted client connections. A separate HTTP listener on port 80 is configured with a permanent (301) redirect to the HTTPS listener, ensuring all client traffic is encrypted in transit. The redirect preserves both path and query string (include_path = true, include_query_string = true). Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000439, CIS Azure 9.1.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: azurerm_application_gateway.main with http_listener (HTTPS on 443, HTTP on 80), redirect_configuration (Permanent redirect to HTTPS), ssl_certificate (dynamic block). Backend traffic from gateway to VM uses HTTP on the app_port within the private VNet.

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary Protection: The Application Gateway v2 is deployed in the public subnet and serves as the sole internet-facing entry point. The Standard_v2 SKU supports WAF v2 upgrade for OWASP rule-based web application filtering. The backend address pool targets the VM private IP only — no direct internet access to the application. The health probe monitors backend availability at configurable intervals (30s interval, 30s timeout, 3 unhealthy threshold) and only routes traffic to healthy backends. The App Gateway NSG permits inbound 80/443 and GatewayManager health probes (65200-65535). Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000364.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: azurerm_application_gateway.main with sku Standard_v2 (upgradeable to WAF_v2), probe block, backend_address_pool targeting var.vm_private_ip. NSG defined in networking module.

implemented-requirements.description: Information Input Validation: The Application Gateway health probe validates backend application responsiveness by sending HTTP requests to a configurable health_check_path at the application port. Backends that fail 3 consecutive health checks (unhealthy_threshold = 3) are removed from the rotation. This ensures only properly functioning application instances receive traffic. The probe validates HTTP response codes to confirm the application is processing requests correctly. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000266.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resource: azurerm_application_gateway.main probe block with host = 127.0.0.1, path = var.health_check_path, interval = 30, timeout = 30, unhealthy_threshold = 3.
